newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda to boost sales of clean cars in US.
newsitem.headline: Honda to boost sales of clean cars in US.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd said on Friday it plans to boost sales of its low emission vehicles (LEVs) in the United States.

Honda plans to launch a series of remodelled Accords, including LEV Accords, this summer in the U.S. and is aiming for sales of the LEV version to account for more than 50 percent of total Accord sales there, a Honda spokesman said.
Honda sells about 400,000 Accord models per year in the United States.
Honda's LEVs have emission levels which are only one-tenth those permitted by present restrictions in the U.S. and Japan.
Carbon monoxide, hydrocarbon and nitrogen oxide levels are far below those set by emission regulations in California, which has particularly strict pollution control measures.
Honda has been selling LEV Civics in the United States since late 1995.
Of its 1996 model Civics, sales of LEV Civics in California accounted for 95.8 percent of total Civic sales of 32,738 units in the year to September 1996.
Honda also plans to offer in the U.S. an Ultra Low Emission Vehicle (ULEV) version of the Accord by end-1997 and Civics which run on compressed natural gas (CNG) in the autumn of 1997.
Emissions from Honda's CNG Civics are cleaner than those from LEVs and ULEVs.
On Wednesday, Toyota Motor Corp, Japan's top car maker, said it would place top priority on offering cleaner cars and technologies.
